messages:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD incident: PROD-DB-CONN-EXHAUST (severity: high) :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: On-call: @alex, this is routed to primary oncall. Auto-escalation in 2m.
alex: acked — looking. seeing lots of `pgbouncer` errors and `max_connections` spikes.
sara: confirming, read from observability: Postgres connection_pool exhausted across primary region, and Redis accept queue spiking. sample logs:```2026-03-15T09:12:40Z pgbouncer[pid]: pooler error: server login failed: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections```
mohit: oof. any traffic pattern? sudden ramp from ingestion workers?
alex: traffic spike from async ingestion batch job 09:10-09:12. looks like a resubmit loop from queueing service.
claire: support report: 3 customers reported slow / errors on search and prompt endpoints. Severity P1 for two customers. Posting IDs to ops channel.
alex: mitigation plan: 1) throttle ingestion workers via feature-flag 2) reduce app pool sizes to free up slots 3) increase pgbouncer pool temporarily 4) enable read-only fallback for non-critical reads
sara: I can patch pgbouncer config and reload. proposed quick change: ```max_client_conn = 20000
default_pool_size = 60 -> 100 (temp)
server_idle_timeout = 60s``` then `systemctl reload pgbouncer`
mohit: before we change pool size, we should force backoff on the job producers — adding 5s sleep between retries. pushing a kill to the runaway worker group now.
alex: nice. @infra-ops can you warm an extra DB replica? we may failover read traffic if primary remains saturated.
infra-ops: starting a read-replica warmup (r5.large) in us-west-2. ETA ~3m. I'll monitor replication lag.
claire: told affected customers: "We're mitigating a database capacity issue, applying throttles and taking steps to reduce load. We'll update in 15 minutes."
sara: pgbouncer reload done. logs show connections freeing up. snippet:```Mar 15 09:14:02 pgbouncer[1234]: INFO server disconnected, clients: 420, servers: 58```
alex: great. still seeing some 502/503s from API gateway for heavy endpoints. adding a temporary rate-limit rule for ingestion route: `ingest.* = 10r/s`
mohit: backoff applied to job producers, one group was stuck in exponential retry loop — fixed and restarted.
pagerduty-bot: @alex acknowledged incident (1799012345)
incidentbot: auto-escalation canceled.
infra-ops: read replica warm and catching up, replication lag 2s. Ready to redirect read traffic.
sara: issuing read-only routing for analytics queries now (feature flag enabled).
alex: monitoring error rate and tail latency. Grafana: 90th p99 token latency returning to baseline, error rate falling.
claire: recording customer impact: 2 enterprise customers impacted for ~12 minutes, partial degradation for others. Will coordinate post-incident comms.
mohit: removing temporary increased pool once stable to avoid resource exhaustion.
sara: reverting `default_pool_size` to normal after 15m. leaving short `server_idle_timeout` change.
alex: postmortem notes to collect: root cause = runaway ingestion job retries causing connection storm; mitigation steps = producer backoff, pgbouncer tuning, replica warm, rate limit; followups = add circuit breaker on ingestion, add alert for sudden client pool surges, improve job dedupe.
claire: creating support ticket for customers affected and scheduling 1:1 followup.
alex: thanks all. I'll leave this thread open for 30m then move to postmortem channel. :thumbsup:
